recipes.name: Spinach Mushroom Quiche
ingredients_raw: 0.5 (8 ounce) package shredded Swiss cheese, divided

steps.text: Gather the ingredients. Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).
Gently combine spinach, mushrooms, onion, and feta cheese in a bowl. Spread mixture into prepared pie crust; top with 1/2 of the Swiss cheese.

Whisk eggs, milk, parsley, garlic, salt, black pepper, and nutmeg in the bowl. Pour egg mixture evenly over filling, swirling egg mixture in bowl to evenly distribute seasonings. Top with remaining Swiss cheese, then place quiche on a baking sheet.
Bake in the preheated oven until lightly puffed and browned, 45 to 50 minutes. A toothpick inserted into the center of the filling should come out clean. Cool for 30 minutes before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Spinach Mushroom Quiche
raw_recipe.description: This spinach mushroom quiche made with fresh spinach, mushrooms, onion, feta, and Swiss cheese makes a flavorful vegetarian breakfast or brunch dish.

review.reviewBody: This is a great recipe, with a nice mix of flavors. I do not have a 9" pie plate, so put it in a 10", but when I got the vegetable mix in it, I wondered how it would ever fit in a 9"! I Agree with the first review; I would fry the onions, mushrooms, and garlic, then wilt the spinach in with it before adding it to the pie plate. I made it exactly like the recipe, and it turned out ok, but I think it would be a little less likely for the cheese to brown and turn tough in the middle if it wasn't so heaped up so high with the raw veggies! It was completely out of the egg mixture for most of the cookiing time.

Doubled the filling and made two pies, one with an almond flour crust from Caroline Ketchum’s cookbook (for the diabetic in the family). Used 1/2 & 1/2 heavy cream/unsweetened almond milk (same reason). Parbaked the crusts first for 10 minutes. Then followed the prior reviewers advice and cooked the mushrooms with chopped onions, garlic, and fresh parsley in some unsalted butter; then wilted the spinach. Blended the spices into the custard, folded in the cheeses (preshredded Swiss-Gruyere mix & precrumbled feta), then layered it all in and baked. Dinner (with salad & berries) was well-liked by all (1 adventurous eater, 1 diabetic, 2 picky adults with different “won’t eats”). The leftovers disappeared by next day lunch. This is a keeper,

The recipe lacks some info, but this quiche was phenomenal! Brown the mushroom slices in a hot pan first, add a little butter, add the onions. Wilt the spinach in a separate pan, drain it and cut it up a bit, add it to the other veg. I added an additional egg, and a sliced tomato on top, but that was it! I've already made this twice and both times it was gone in 24 hrs! For one I was out of feta and used shredded colby jack instead (I don't like swiss) and it was still phenomenal. Oh and bake it in a cast iron skillet if you have one!

After reading reviews I decided to try this with some farm fresh eggs I had just received. I used two Pilsbury pie crusts and baked them as instructed on the box. I then put one layer of sliced swiss cheese on the bottom of the pie crust. I browned some sausage and then sautéed the fresh mushrooms with a bag of fresh baby spinach and some chopped garlic, added some frozen seasoning blend (onion, bell pepper and celery, what we call the "trinity" in Louisiana). I drained all the water and mixed in the sausage and then layered the mixture in my two pie shells with the cheese (I used Swiss and Garlic and Herb Feta). I also added a little sweet basil and skipped the other seasonings. I poured my egg mixture over and then layered some sliced Roma tomatoes and another layer of cheese. The best thing about this recipe is that you can pretty much change it up most any way and it will be good. The quiche baked perfectly and we thought it was delicious! I will definitely try it again with probably some different veggies and we like meat in ours as well.

I was w/o feta, so I subbed with some ricotta and parm, had no problems fitting it all in the pan and still had a good 1/2 of space left, and also used double the spinach! The only crust I could Imagine this not fitting in is those shallow ready frozen ones that in a pinch bought by accident and noticed after getting home they had shrunk like all other products! Those looking for an easier fix should try this, put all your veggies in a bowl, drizzle and mix with some good evoo, cover tightly with plastic wrap and microwave for 4-5 minutes, I tossed it up and added spinach halfway through. And if going through the motions of making it yourself, do yourself a favor and buy those rolled up refrigerated pie crust and a couple of (deep dish) glass pie plates. I got a two pack at aldi not long ago for $3.99, no prebake needed as long as it goes on the rack, pie crust really shouldn't be baked on a cookie sheet. If using these for a double layer, brush with egg or milk, and they can pass as homemade.

I sautéed the onion and bacon bits with the mushrooms and at the last 5 min added the spinach. Pre baked the pie shell for about 10min at 350. Dumped all the sauté into the pie shell added Swiss cheese to the egg mixture. This cuts down on the water released by the shrooms and spinach and results in a firmer set.

I made my first pie crust (fabulous!) two nights before making this quiche (also my first). I followed the recipe but since my husband had hidden the Swiss cheese, I had to make do with smoked Gouda, crumbled feta and extra sharp cheddar. Like many others here, I sauteed the mushrooms, onions and spinach and let the mixture cool before adding to my freshly-baked & cooled pie crust. I even forgot to add the milk to the whisked eggs. But this recipe came out AMAZING! I only had to bake it for about 25 minutes because of the omitted milk, but it baked up perfectly and was so incredibly tasty, I will be making this again and again.

OK I browned the onions and mushrooms first and then wilted down the spinach all in the same pan then added the mix to pie and topped with the cheese. I used gruyere and aged gouda (Old Amsterdam) cheese - no Feta. Followed the recipe to the "T" after that... So easy and elegant. Luv the leftovers for quick breakfast!

I love this recipe so much! I also cook the veggies before and mix with the feta. I double the egg mixture and then divide the mixture bc it is a LOT for one 9 in. pan. It always is a hit with my family.
Prepping the veggies it was obvious it wouldn't fit no matter what. Sautéed everything first, and used about 3/4 of the veggie mix. Increased eggs from 4 to 6. That ratio seemed to work well for me.

I made this recipe twice, once following the instructions strictly and the second time cooking the veggies before assembling the quiche. The 1st cook was quiche soup and I felt bad for my crust. The quiche I made with cooked veggies was a triumph. Two stars for the recipe as written, 5 stars for the cooked veggies quiche.

I loved that this recipe called for fresh spinach. So, I got baby fresh spinach. Like others did, I sauteed the mushrooms, onions, and garlic (in a tiny bit of EVOO) and wilted the spinach. I also replaced the cheeses with (my favorite) Gruyère. It turned out beautifully, and all were pleased with the taste!
Made as per the recipe (no advance sauteeing) and it was delicious!

Been making this quiche for I don't know how many years, and it's always a big hit. It's become a staple of family gatherings! Just one note- SAUTE THE VEGGIES, otherwise the recipe doesn't really make sense. You want to do onions, then shrooms, then wilt the spinach, then combine in a bowl with the rest. This makes it so you won't have leftover filling or raw veggies. Mushrooms and onions are not going to cook from raw inside a quiche.
I wish I had read the reviews before making this. But I will try again, cooking the veggies first .
Feta does not work in quiche for my taste

I thought this recipe was great. Few adjustments for me. I chopped up the mushrooms and sautéed them with the garlic. I also chopped the spinach up and in a large bowl, seasoned it and tossed the shredded cheese blend with it. This will be breakfast for me and I wanted a little more ooomph so I cooked up Jimmy dean country mild sausage crumbles and mixed it with the shrooms before assembling in the crust. Sprinkled some more shredded cheese blend on top. Mine baked for 47 min of perfect (for me) Will for sure make again.

I changed this recipe. I summered the onion, mushroom, and garlic. I seasoned it as it was cooking. I added the chopped up spinach and let it cook. I turned off the burner and covered the veggies. I scammed 4 eggs. Added the cheese , and a scoop of cottage cheese to the eggs and mixed it well. I put the veggies in a jiffy unbacked pit shell. I poured the egg mixture over the veggies. I backed the quiche for 55 min at 350° It is beautiful and tasts great.

I have made this countless times without modifications and it turns out great. The only thing is that I chop the Spinach really fine and I have to pack it into the crust because it is a lot. I have used a deep-dish pie plate (which really isn't 9") and regular pie plates (most times) and both turn out well. That being said, my only "complaint" is that the veggies seem to float to the top of the custard during baking so it is not a homogeneous filling. Adding more eggs makes it worse, not better. I was thinking about trying pre-cooking the custard until it begins to thicken, then stirring the vegetables into the hot custard before putting everything into the pie shell. Has anyone tried this method? Any other suggestions?
This quiche was so delicious! Instead of Swiss cheese, I used a block of cheddar-gruyere.
